::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [August 1873]  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell
:::

My dear [Miss Poole](people/person_1187.qmd)[^1]
I suspected that you would have to change to Monday. I wonder if the enclosed will make any further change.  We shall be very glad to have you here on Sunday, and the carriage with [Miss Mackenzie](people/person_930.qmd) in it will meet you at Bpstoke at the same time.

I suppose - as you do not say so - [Miss Dyson](people/person_464.qmd) has heard no more from Heaths Court[^2]

yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Endorsed in pencil ‘Aug. 1873/ authoress’.
[^2]: Presumed to be addressed to Harriet Poole, governess and sister of the Gosling Alice Poole.
[^3]: Heath's Court was the home of Sir [John Taylor Coleridge](people/person_344.qmd).
